recipes.name: Apple Rhubarb Crisp
ingredients_raw: 1 cup chilled butter, cut into pieces
2 tablespoons white sugar, or to taste

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Butter a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Mix apples, rhubarb, 1 cup white sugar, 1/4 cup flour, and 1 teaspoon cinnamon in a bowl until thoroughly combined. Spread fruit mixture into the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Mix oats, remaining 1 ½ cups flour, and brown sugar in a separate bowl; cut in butter until crumbly. Spread evenly over fruit mixture.
Mix 2 tablespoons white sugar with remaining 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in a small bowl; sprinkle over oat topping.
Bake in the preheated oven until fruit is bubbling and thick and topping is golden brown, about 45 minutes. Let cool 10 to 15 minutes, then serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Rhubarb Crisp
raw_recipe.description: This apple-rhubarb crisp pairs tangy rhubarb with sweet, fruity apples and tops it all off with a crumbly topping of brown sugar, butter, and oats.

review.reviewBody: Very tasty and worth doing. I prefer to have somewhat "measurable" quantities - 6 apples can vary so much. I used 3 cups chopped rhubarb and 5 cups chopped apple (peeled) for my pan; and the taste was just right for our family.

We like a higher fruit to crumble ratio so I used 3 apples and 3 lbs of frozen rhubarb that I thawed and drained. I added 1/2 cup each of flour and sugar to the fruit with 1 tsp cinnamon. For the rolled oat mixture I reduced the brown sugar and butter to 3/4 cup each, keeping the oats and flour the same, used white whole wheat for the all purpose, and added another tsp of cinnamon instead of sprinkling cinnamon sugar over the top. Mine baked in 45 minutes exactly. Crisps and crumbles are easily costumized to your tastes, this recipe just had way too much sugar for us, we like the tartness of rhubarb. I made this for #AllrecipesAllstarsCanada #AppleHarvest

I cut the recipe in half, because I’m currently using a counter top oven/fryer. (My oven is broken). 
Otherwise I made it as written. About 2.5 cups of apples and a little over 1/3 cup of rhubarb. It is really good. 
Next time I will add a few more apples to change the topping apple ratio. But it is really super as written. 
Thanks for a keeper of a recipe.
I only used 5 apples and used 2 cups of rhubarb, it really enhances the flavour and makes it more of a crowd pleaser.

Reading reviews I did some major altering but this recipe gave me the basis for developing this combo of fruits...I used about 3 cups of thinly sliced rhubarb from garden and 5 cups of un-named apple from our tree...cut sugar back on all and only used about half the topping...Incredible combo and will hope to replicate again...

Definitely will make this again. I had to use King Arthur Flour gluten free flour blend. I made half a recipe in 8x8 pan. For fruit used 3 1/2c apples and 2c rhubarb. Used half recipe of crisp with 1/2 amount of sugar. Thanks for s sharing such a versatile recipe.

Great recipe! However, I did adjust some things! First, I only put about half a cup of white sugar on the diced fruit while doubling the cinnamon. Second, I only put half a cup of brown sugar in the flour mixture. It was delicious and still sweet enough. Served it with vanilla ice cream and it was a hit. Also took the advice of someone else and did 3C rhubarb and 5C apples.

I made it as written, just without being too precise on the fruit quantity. I found the sugar quantities were okay, especially with the tartness of the rhubarb and baking to please a crowd. I used frozen apples and rhubarb, draining out excess liquid. If sliced, rather than diced, definitely peel the apples or the peel gets stringy. For 12 cups of chopped fruit, I double the flour coating and crumb topping.

5c apples (cameo & Fuji), almost 3c rhubarb and I halved the sugar and flour everywhere. Used allspice instead of cinnamon. Should have omitted the sugar on the topping, it was a tad too much. Bust fantastic recipe!!!

If I ever try it again I’ll cover it with tin foil when I cook it to keep moisture in. Right now I’ve got a dried fruit and oatmeal mess. The fruit never got “bubbly” and the oatmeal never got crispy.

It was so easy to make, and I made 4 pans and froze it after baking. Everybody that tried it loved It. I actually doubled the rhubarb to 2 cups as I wanted to taste it also, no change to sugar amount, but I used stevia.
I reduced the white sugar to half a cup and saved the sugar to sprinkle over the top from it but it was still too sweet, even for my husband who has an exaggerated sweet tooth…. .

Far,FAR too much flour in this recipe,,I’ve made apple and rhubarb crisp for over 26 years now and can make it in my sleep,,,Never have I Ever used more than 1/4 cup of flour,,,and ONLY because we live higher above sea level here in North Western Alberta,Canada.
really easy, adn quick to prepare
That was the best Crisp I've ever made. Going to make it again soon!

Too sweet and I have a major sweet tooth. I cut the white sugar in half and still found this to be overwhelming. I should’ve cut the brown sugar in half as well. Interesting choice to not peel the apples—I don’t think I’ll do that again, but it wasn’t the worst part about this dish. If it was being served with a lightly sweetened whipped cream it might be okay as I made it but with ice cream it was just overkill. Unbalanced. Still looking for the perfect apple rhubarb crisp.
Easy peasy! Loved the addition of the cinnamon sugar topping!

Very easy to make, and the result was a harmonious sweet and tart blend. The crispy topping added just the right texture to the warm, fruity filling. I served it while still hot, paired with a scoop of ice cream, and it was pure comfort on a plate.
Best crumble ever, according to everyone we shared with! We added nutmeg and doubled the cinnamon
My family enjoyed this recipe and really liked the topping. It was enough topping so the recipe didn't go soggy. Thank you.
